newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy communists warn of four problem areas ahead.
newsitem.headline: Italy communists warn of four problem areas ahead.

text.p: The leader of the hardline Communist Refoundation party allied to Italy's ruling centre-left coalition said on Thursday that the government had to resolve four major issues in 1997.

Fausto Bertinotti, opening the party's third national congress in Rome, said the problem areas facing Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government were "revenue, contractual defence of labour, the welfare state and employment."
Bertinotti, with Prodi also attending the meeting, repeated his party's support for the government, while saying it was a relationship that was adjusted in relation to the achievement of agreed aims.
He said it would be "unpardonable" to allow the centre-right to regain power in Italy.
Centre-right leader Silvio Berlusconi was prime minister in a short-lived government in 1994 before he was toppled when the separatist Northern League party left his coalition.

His government was followed by a non-elected technocrat administration led by current Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, who held power until the end of 1995 and remained as caretaker until a general election in April this year.

Communist Refoundation holds the balance of power in the lower house of parliament and, despite voting with the government, has refused to join the ranks of the coalition adopting "critical and autonomous" backing instead.

Bertinotti said Refoundation, born as a breakaway faction after the old Italian Communist Party (PCI) changed its name to the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), had succeeded in its battle to become Italy's new communist party.
"The battle for the existence of a new communist party in Italy has been won," he declared, saying that Refoundation was an "anti-capitalist" party aimed at social change.
At the same time Bertinotti spoke of a need for dialogue "between all critical views in the world".
He said the Roman Catholic Church in particular had offered "material for thought, research and dialogue".
"When Pope John Paul says that the supremacy of the market cannot be accepted because it produces new poverty and unemployment, he speaks critically of the capitalism of our times," Bertinotti said.
